svg.text: Setup 1 "Sweep" — applying it to YOUR switch
Orientation, meter procedure, per-lug checklist and solder order · sheet 3 of 3
A · HOW TO HOLD THE SWITCH
lug tabs facing YOU · 24 of them, two rows of 12
Lugs toward you, mounting ears left and right, lever slot across the middle.
The TOP row of 12 is layer 1 (poles 1 and 2); the BOTTOM row is layer 2 (poles 3, 4).
Each row is two poles of six: a common at the OUTER end, then positions 5-4-3-2-1
counting INWARD. The two position-1 lugs of a row sit next to each other in the middle.
If your lugs face away from you the drawing mirrors left-to-right. That is fine —
step B settles it, and step B always wins over the picture.
B · PROVE IT WITH A METER (do this first, always)
Probe two lugs in the same group of six.
Find the four COMMONS. A common is the lug that beeps to
exactly one other lug in its group in EVERY lever position.
There are four, one per group, at the outer corners.
Set the blade fully toward the BRIDGE.
Hold one probe on a common; find the lug that beeps.
That lug is POSITION 1 of that pole. Mark it.
Move the lever one detent toward the neck at a time,
Repeat for all four commons. Masking tape and a pen.
From here on use YOUR marks, not the factory numbers.
The #n numbers on sheet 2 are the manufacturer's; they
are a cross-check, not the authority. Your marks win.
C · CONNECTION CHECKLIST — every one of the 24 lugs
common = your marked C (factory #1) → volume lug 3 (OUT bus)
common = your marked C (factory #12) → volume DPDT lug A2
common = your marked C (factory #13) → volume DPDT lug B2
common = your marked C (factory #24) → ground buss
At the pickups: join bridge RED+WHITE, join neck WHITE+RED.
Solder, heatshrink, done. These never reach the switch as two wires.
Tin all 24 lugs you will use. Skip pole 3 positions 1 and 5.
Fit the on-switch jumpers first, while access is good:
W1 across P1 1-3-4 · W2 P1-2 to P2-1 to P2-4 · W3 P2-2 to P2-3 to P4-1
W4 P1-5 to P3-2 to P3-3 · W5 P2-5 to P3-4 to P4-2 · W6 across P4 3-4-5
Now land the six pickup leads, one net at a time. Tick the boxes in C.
Four commons to volume lug 3, DPDT A2, DPDT B2, ground.
DPDT internals, then pots, tone cap, treble bleed, jack, ground buss.
Test on the bench (panel E) BEFORE it goes in the guitar.
Meter across the jack tip and sleeve, volume wide open, tone wide open.
Expected DC resistance, for a matched ~8 k pair:
Any position reading OPEN or near 0 Ω is a wiring fault — find it now.
Position 3 volume-down must be roughly double any single-pickup reading;
that is the proof the both-humbuckers-in-series chain is intact.
ORIENTATION IS THE ONE THING THIS SHEET CANNOT KNOW.
Whether position 1 sits at the left or right end depends on how the switch is mounted. Panel B settles it in five minutes and is authoritative.
Sheet 1 = harness overview · sheet 2 = the switch as wired · this sheet = how to transfer it to the part in your hand.
Crossing wires are NOT connected unless a solid junction dot is shown.
